title: The Boy Bathing
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Boy was bathing in a river and got out of his depth, and was in great danger of being drowned. A man who was passing along a road heard his cries for help, and went to the riverside and began to scold him for being so careless as to get into deep water, but made no attempt to help him. "Oh, sir," cried the Boy, "please help me first and scold me afterwards." Give assistance, not advice, in a crisis.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Boy bathing?
options: In a lake
In the sea
In a pond
In a river

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Boy while bathing?
options: He was bitten by a fish
He got out of his depth and was in great danger of drowning
He got tangled in weeds near the shore
He was swept downstream by a strong current

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who heard the Boy's cries for help?
options: A man passing along a road
A fisherman in a boat
Another boy swimming nearby
A shepherd tending his flock

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the man do instead of helping the Boy?
options: Ran to fetch a rope
Called for more people to help
Scolded him for being careless and made no attempt to help
Jumped in immediately to save him

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "depth" mean in "got out of his depth"?
options: A type of swimming stroke
The temperature of the water
A measurement of distance along the shore
Water too deep for him to stand or manage safely

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "scold" mean in "began to scold him"?
options: To criticize sharply for a fault
To praise warmly
To ignore completely
To laugh at playfully

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Boy's plea a pointed criticism of the man's behavior?
options: It proves the man does not know how to swim
It reveals the Boy no longer wants to be rescued
It shows the man is more focused on judging the Boy's mistake than on saving his life
It shows the Boy thinks the man caused the danger

questions.prompt: Which statement, made explicit at the end of the passage, best captures the point of the fable?
options: Boys should learn to swim before bathing alone
Give assistance, not advice, in a crisis
Passersby are never responsible for helping strangers
Scolding is the best way to teach caution

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Boy use to plead with the man?
options: "Please save me before I drown!"
"Why won't you jump in and rescue me?"
"I promise I will never swim here again"
"Please help me first and scold me afterwards"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the man do upon hearing the Boy's cries?
options: Went to the riverside and began to scold him
Ran to find a rope
Called out for other help
Ignored the cries and kept walking

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "careless" mean in "so careless as to get into deep water"?
options: Extremely skilled
Unusually brave
Not paying enough attention to danger
Deliberately reckless for attention

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "cries" mean in "heard his cries for help"?
options: Tears of sadness
Loud calls of distress
Songs sung quietly
Written messages

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what general principle about responding to emergencies does the fable illustrate?
options: Advice should always come before action
Bystanders should never get involved in others' problems
Scolding is an effective way to prevent danger
Practical help matters more in the moment than criticism or lessons

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Boy in danger of drowning asks a scolding bystander to help him first and lecture him later
A drowning Boy is rescued immediately by a passing man
A Boy scolds a man for swimming carelessly
A man teaches a Boy how to swim safely
